title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative: The post-Covid environment prompted the Lao National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LNCCI) to address an unprecedented demand - reinforcing its policy advocacy to channel the private sector’s needs to the government. In 2023, LNCCI organized an event called the Lao Business Forum (LBF) with the theme of “Re-building Better”. The goal was to establish a policy platform that could drive investment and job creation. In preparing for the LBF, LNCCI conducted a survey involving 150 large and medium-sized enterprises across key industries. This survey captured enterprise perspectives on labour law, challenges and potential solutions. Drawing on the survey, LNCCI formulated policy recommendations. These recommendations encompassed critical areas such as transparent management of skills development funds, gender equality in retirement age, employment contracts and social security benefits. The recommendations were presented at the LBF in March 2023, with the participation of the Prime Minister of Lao DPR. This effort worked to establish consistent interpretation of laws and eliminate barriers to private sector investment. In June 2023, the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare met with LNCCI to incorporate employers’ recommendations into new policies and legislation, in response to the outcomes of the LBF. In line with its broader strategy to enhance policy influence, LNCCI forged a framework agreement on bipartite social dialogue with the Lao Federation of Trade Unions (LFTU) in May 2022. Solidifying this partnership, they agreed in May 2023 to conduct regular meetings. These meetings would serve as a platform to address issues on labour legislation, skills development and social protection. To elevate the quality of its policy submissions, LNCCI set up a Policy Advisory Committee in June 2023 composed of experts and academics. The committee embarked on a survey to identify skills gap and subsequently formulated policy recommendations concerning TVET. The ILO equipped the LNCCI secretariat with the skills necessary for designing and administering surveys, as well as crafting policy recommendations. This empowered LNCCI to undertake similar projects independently. To enhance LNCCI’s engagement in policy advocacy, the ILO lent support to the establishment of the LNCCI Policy Advisory Committee. This Committee convenes regularly to discuss policy matters and contributes insights to evidence-based position papers for policy advocacy. To facilitate policy advocacy through social dialogue, the ILO held bipartite social dialogue workshops in collaboration with LFTU during 2022 and 2023. These workshops aimed to formulate policy recommendations to be presented to the government. The ILO also provided training to LNCCI staff in 2023, covering strategic advocacy and effective influence techniques (such as lobbying and negotiation), communication skills for advocacy (including writing policy position papers, generating post-position paper content like news articles, press releases, feature writing, copywriting), and leveraging digital advocacy through social media. This comprehensive effort strengthened LNCCI’s capacity to advocate for policy reforms that contribute to an improved business environment. Furthermore, LNCCI's ability to systematically and consistently engage with the government and other tripartite bodies has been greatly enhanced.
